patients.summary: Retail cashier turned high school science teacher with hypertension on HCTZ, obesity and varicose veins who joins in 2021. Chronic low back pain and chronic venous insufficiency in 2023, abnormal bleeding with a benign biopsy, then an unexpected first pregnancy at 48 delivered in May 2024. Right plantar fasciitis in 2025 and right-leg cellulitis in January 2026, recurring in August 2026 with a hospital admission.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Ms. Keegan phoned about membership. Her old primary care office is cutting hours and she wants a doctor she can actually reach. Explained the membership and that insurance still covers labs and specialists. Booked new patient visit 9/14 at 8:40. Release of information form emailed for her prior office; she will sign and return today. Reminded her to bring her pill bottles.

documents.title: Prior primary care records
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Faxed records, 23 pages, from the patient's previous family practice, covering 2015 to 2021.

Problem list on their summary: essential hypertension (on treatment since about 2017), obesity, varicose veins of both legs. Status post laparoscopic cholecystectomy around 2011.
Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Last office BP on file 130/82. Weight 192 lb at the last visit.
Pap 2019 negative per their note. Last labs 2020: BMP normal, potassium 4.1.
Immunizations: COVID-19 Pfizer x2, March and April 2021. Tdap 2013.

Filed to chart. Reviewed for the new patient visit.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
46 yo woman new to me. Previous office records reviewed (faxed 9/8).

HTN since roughly 2017, on HCTZ 25 every morning, doesn't check at home. No headaches, chest pain, palpitations. Weight has been her struggle for about ten years; she's tried a couple of commercial programs. Varicose veins both legs for years, mother has the same. Legs ache a bit after long shifts but no real swelling she's noticed.

PSH: lap chole ~age 35.
Meds: HCTZ 25 daily. Allergies: none to medications.
FHx: mother HTN and varicose veins. Father obese with type 2 DM. Maternal aunt had endometrial cancer at 50.
Social: works the register at a grocery store, long hours on her feet. Lives with her partner. Never smoked. A drink or two a month. Periods regular. Never pregnant.
COVID vaccines x2 this spring. Tdap 2013.

Exam: vitals as charted, BMI 32. Well appearing. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, healed lap scars. Legs: scattered varicosities on both calves, no edema, skin intact, pulses good.

A/P
1. HTN: at goal on HCTZ. CMP today for K and Cr.
2. Obesity, BMI 32: talked through food and activity in broad terms; she'd like to revisit once she's settled in. A1c and lipids today given father's diabetes.
3. Varicose veins: asymptomatic, observe.
4. Health maintenance: due for colon screening at 46, GI referral placed. Screening mammogram ordered. HCV and HIV one-time screens with today's draw. Flu and COVID booster at a nurse visit next month. Pap last 2019, normal; due next year.
Follow up 6 months for BP.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Andrea, all of your blood work from Tuesday looks good. Kidney function and potassium are normal on the water pill, A1c is in the normal range, cholesterol is fine, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens are negative. Nothing to change. Gastroenterology should be calling you about the colonoscopy.

documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here after work for flu and COVID booster. Booster eligibility reviewed per current guidance (BMI over 30). Flu L deltoid, Pfizer booster R deltoid, both tolerated. Observed 15 min, no reaction. BP checked while here, see vitals. VIS given.

reports.text: Bilateral digital screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. No prior studies available for comparison. The breasts are heterogeneously dense, which may obscure small masses. No suspicious mass, architectural distortion or suspicious calcifications in either breast. Skin and axillae unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: BI-RADS 1, negative. Routine screening in one year.

documents.title: Mammogram result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Screening mammogram negative, BI-RADS 1. Dense tissue noted. Letter to patient via portal. Repeat next fall.

documents.title: Screening colonoscopy report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology group. Procedure date 11/18/2021.
Indication: first screening colonoscopy, age 46, no family history of colon cancer.
Allergies: NKDA. Medications: hydrochlorothiazide.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care. Prep: good (Boston-type score 8 of 9 per report).
Findings: scope advanced to the cecum, appendiceal orifice photographed. Mucosa normal throughout. No polyps, no diverticula. Small internal hemorrhoids on retroflexion.
Impression: normal screening colonoscopy.
Recommendation: next screening colonoscopy in 10 years.

documents.title: HCTZ refill
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Electronic request from her pharmacy, previous prescriber's script out of refills. HCTZ 25 mg #90 with 3 refills sent under PCP per protocol. BMP 9/2021 normal.

documents.title: Follow-up: hypertension
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Six-month BP check. Taking HCTZ most mornings, misses maybe one a week when she opens early. No lightheadedness or cramps. Busy winter at the store. Not much exercise.
O: BP and weight per vitals. Heart RRR. No leg edema; varicosities unchanged.
A/P: HTN at goal. Continue HCTZ 25. BMP today. Suggested pairing the pill with her morning coffee. Weight: she is interested in walking with her partner once the weather turns; we'll revisit. Physical in the summer; Pap due then.

documents.title: BMP result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Andrea, your potassium, sodium and kidney numbers are all normal. Keep going with the HCTZ as you are. See you this summer for your physical.

reports.text: ThinPrep liquid-based cervical cytology. Specimen adequate, transformation zone component present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV DNA not detected.
reports.conclusion: NILM, HPV negative. Co-testing interval 5 years.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 46F.

Interval: no new issues. Walking some evenings with her partner, irregularly. Still on her feet all day at work. Periods regular, monthly. No breast concerns. Sleeping ok. PHQ-9 2.

Meds: HCTZ 25 daily. NKDA. Never smoker, rare alcohol.

Exam: vitals as charted. HEENT normal. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart and lungs normal. Breasts symmetric, no masses, no nipple discharge, axillae clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix normal in appearance, Pap with HPV collected; bimanual unremarkable. Legs with varicosities, no edema. Skin without suspicious lesions.

A/P
- HTN: at goal. CMP.
- Obesity: weight stable. Encouraged the walking, 30 minutes most days, and fewer meals out of the break room vending machine.
- Preventive: Pap/HPV today. Colonoscopy 2021 normal, next 2031. Mammogram this fall. Lipids and A1c today. Flu and the new COVID booster in September.
Return 6-8 months for BP, physical next summer.

documents.title: Pap smear and labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news: your Pap smear is normal and the HPV test is negative, so you won't need another one for five years. Cholesterol, sugar (A1c) and kidney tests from your physical are all normal too.

documents.title: Flu and COVID bivalent
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Flu vaccine and Pfizer bivalent booster given, one in each arm. Pt denies prior reactions. Waited 15 minutes, fine. Next mammogram reminder given, she will call radiology to schedule.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis, compared with the October 2021 study. Heterogeneously dense breast tissue. No new mass, distortion or suspicious calcification. Stable appearance bilaterally.

documents.title: Mammogram 2022
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Negative, stable. Patient notified through the portal.

documents.title: HCTZ renewal
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy asking for new HCTZ 25 mg script, last refill used. Seen 7/2022 with normal CMP. Renewed #90 x3 per protocol.
